judged_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` compares `cal.externalId` against `externalCalendarId` inside the branch where `externalCalendarId` is already known to be falsy, so the `.find()` can never match and `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` (and the identical pattern at line 317 in `deleteEvent`) always resolve to `undefined` instead of falling back to the booking's destination calendar, breaking calendar update/delete routing for legacy bookings that lack a stored `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the else-branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), so `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can’t match any real calendar externalId, resulting in `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becoming `undefined` instead of falling back to a destination calendar (previous behavior was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This would mis-route/ break update/delete when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided.
